# prism-models Specification

<!-- Generated by Prism from prism/spec.json. Change the app through your agent with /prism, not by editing this file. -->

## Purpose

Prism Models: Decides whether one language or reasoning model routed into the Prism from a hub such as Hugging Face may be fetched or run in the owner's browser, so that only a model pinned by revision and hash, in a format with a locked runtime, granted by the owner, runs, and nothing moves while the Prism is halted.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Never run when halted is yes

The app SHALL NOT answer `run` when halted is yes, because a halted Prism would still compute.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-001, theorem `inv001Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-001 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `locked onnx match match granted yes` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `run`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: Never fetch when halted is yes

The app SHALL NOT answer `fetch` when halted is yes, because a halted Prism would still move bytes.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-002, theorem `inv002Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-002 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `locked onnx match match granted yes` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `fetch`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: Never run when source is unlocked

The app SHALL NOT answer `run` when source is unlocked, because a model nobody pinned could be swapped upstream.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-003, theorem `inv003Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-003 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `unlocked onnx match match granted no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `run`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: Never fetch when source is unlocked

The app SHALL NOT answer `fetch` when source is unlocked, because bytes nobody pinned could be anything.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-004, theorem `inv004Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-004 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `unlocked onnx match match granted no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `fetch`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: Never run when route is ungranted

The app SHALL NOT answer `run` when route is ungranted, because a model the owner never granted would read the owner's content.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-005, theorem `inv005Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-005 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `locked onnx match match ungranted no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `run`
- **AND** the app answers `ask`, decided by REQ-006

### Requirement: Never fetch when route is ungranted

The app SHALL NOT answer `fetch` when route is ungranted, because bytes would be moved for a model the owner never granted.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-006, theorem `inv006Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-006 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `locked onnx match match ungranted no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `fetch`
- **AND** the app answers `ask`, decided by REQ-006

### Requirement: Never run when runtime is not match

The app SHALL NOT answer `run` when runtime is not match, because unverified runtime bytes could compute anything.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-007, theorem `inv007Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-007 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `locked onnx mismatch match granted no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `run`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-004

### Requirement: Never run when weights is not match

The app SHALL NOT answer `run` when weights is not match, because unverified weights would answer as if they were the locked model.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-008, theorem `inv008Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-008 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `locked onnx match mismatch granted no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `run`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-005

### Requirement: Never run when format is other

The app SHALL NOT answer `run` when format is other, because a format without a locked runtime would run on unverified code.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-009, theorem `inv009Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-009 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `locked other match match granted no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `run`
- **AND** the app answers `refuse`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: REQ-001 refuse when halted is yes

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when halted is yes, because the kill switch stops every model.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule1`).

#### Scenario: REQ-001 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `locked onnx match match granted yes` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: REQ-002 refuse when source is unlocked

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when source is unlocked and no earlier rule matches, because only a model pinned by revision and hash is routed into the Prism.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule2`).

#### Scenario: REQ-002 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `unlocked onnx match match granted no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: REQ-003 refuse when format is other

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when format is other and no earlier rule matches, because the Prism runs only a format it holds a locked runtime for.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule3`).

#### Scenario: REQ-003 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `locked other match match granted no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: REQ-004 refuse when runtime is mismatch

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when runtime is mismatch and no earlier rule matches, because runtime bytes that differ from the lock could compute anything.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule4`).

#### Scenario: REQ-004 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `locked onnx mismatch match granted no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`, decided by REQ-004

### Requirement: REQ-005 refuse when weights is mismatch

The app SHALL answer `refuse` when weights is mismatch and no earlier rule matches, because weights that differ from the lock are not the model the owner granted.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule5`).

#### Scenario: REQ-005 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `locked onnx match mismatch granted no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `refuse`, decided by REQ-005

### Requirement: REQ-006 ask when route is ungranted

The app SHALL answer `ask` when route is ungranted and no earlier rule matches, because the owner decides which models are routed into the Prism.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule6`).

#### Scenario: REQ-006 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `locked onnx match match ungranted no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `ask`, decided by REQ-006

### Requirement: REQ-007 fetch when runtime is missing

The app SHALL answer `fetch` when runtime is missing and no earlier rule matches, because the locked runtime is fetched from this page, checked, then kept.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule7`).

#### Scenario: REQ-007 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `locked onnx missing match granted no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `fetch`, decided by REQ-007

### Requirement: REQ-008 fetch when weights is missing

The app SHALL answer `fetch` when weights is missing and no earlier rule matches, because the locked weights are fetched from this page, checked, then kept.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule8`).

#### Scenario: REQ-008 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `locked onnx match missing granted no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `fetch`, decided by REQ-008

### Requirement: Otherwise run

The app SHALL answer `run` when no rule matches, because a pinned model with verified runtime and weights, granted by the owner, runs locally.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: No rule matches

- **WHEN** the request is `locked onnx match match granted no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `run`

### Requirement: The first matching rule decides

The app SHALL try REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-007, REQ-008 in that order, and the first rule that matches SHALL decide.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: Two rules match

- **WHEN** the request is `locked gguf missing missing granted no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `fetch`, decided by REQ-007, the earlier rule

### Requirement: Request and answers

The app SHALL read one request as one line of 6 fields separated by single spaces, in this order, and SHALL answer exactly one of `run`, `fetch`, `ask`, `refuse`, or `invalid` for anything else.

| Field | Accepts | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | `locked`, `unlocked` | whether the model's hub, repository, revision and every file it loads are pinned by SHA-256 in the models lock |
| `format` | `onnx`, `gguf`, `other` | the standard the model's weights are written in: ONNX, GGUF, or anything else |
| `runtime` | `match`, `mismatch`, `missing` | whether the runtime bytes for that format (the ONNX or GGUF engine), read back from the browser store, equal the ones in the lock |
| `weights` | `match`, `mismatch`, `missing` | whether the model's weight and tokenizer files, read back from the browser store, equal the ones in the lock |
| `route` | `granted`, `ungranted` | whether the owner's grant names this model as one routed into the Prism |
| `halted` | `no`, `yes` | whether the owner's kill switch has halted the Prism |

| Answer | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `run` | run the model on locally held, verified bytes |
| `fetch` | fetch the missing locked bytes from this page, check them, and keep them in the browser |
| `ask` | ask the owner whether to route this model into the Prism |
| `refuse` | run and fetch nothing, and say why |
| `invalid` | the request is malformed |

Verified: reading a request is tested, not proved.

#### Scenario: A malformed request is invalid

- **WHEN** the request is not 6 fields in this order
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `invalid`

## Examples

- `locked onnx match match granted no` gives `run`
- `locked gguf match match granted no` gives `run`
- `locked onnx match match granted yes` gives `refuse`
- `unlocked onnx match match granted no` gives `refuse`
- `locked other match match granted no` gives `refuse`
- `locked onnx mismatch match granted no` gives `refuse`
- `locked onnx match mismatch granted no` gives `refuse`
- `locked onnx match match ungranted no` gives `ask`
- `locked onnx missing match granted no` gives `fetch`
- `locked onnx match missing granted no` gives `fetch`
- `locked gguf missing missing granted no` gives `fetch`
- `locked onnx missing missing ungranted no` gives `ask`
- `locked onnx mismatch missing ungranted no` gives `refuse`
- `unlocked gguf missing missing ungranted yes` gives `refuse`

## What is proved and what is tested

Lean proves each property marked proved above, for every request that decodes, with no exceptions and no sampling. The proof is about `judge`, the function the WebAssembly guest runs, because both come from the same model.

The parsing of requests is tested, not proved: the acceptance vectors in the app replay through the built guest, including malformed and oversized requests.

Nothing here says the rules are the right rules. That is the part only you can judge.

## Files

- `prism/spec.json` is this spec as data.
- `src/PrismModels.lex.tex` is the LexLean model generated from it. It is the single source of the app.
